text: You are in danger of living a life so comfortable and soft that you will die without ever realizing your true potential.
context: The situation line of the warning order that opens Can't Hurt Me, before the introduction.

text: Denial is the ultimate comfort zone.
context: The second sentence of the introduction. Believing you already know yourself, he writes, is not the same as it being true.

text: Don't stop when you are tired. Stop when you are done.
context: An execution step in the same warning order. The mission, he writes, is to unshackle the mind, not to feel better.
From the introduction. A pep talk, he writes, is a temporary fix and will not rewire the brain.

text: But the truth is we all make habitual, self-limiting choices.
context: He calls the pattern as natural as a sunset and as fundamental as gravity, which is why he says motivation is useless.

text: Only you can master your mind, which is what it takes to live a bold life filled with accomplishments most people consider beyond their capability.
context: His own sentence in the introduction, after he tells of an MIT panel on genetic ceilings. He is not quoting the professor or Heraclitus here.

text: There will always be the 1 percent of us who are willing to put in the work to defy the odds.
context: What he says he told the MIT professor who argued that mental toughness stops at a genetic ceiling.

text: Our governor is buried deep in our minds, intertwined with our very identity.
context: From the 40% Rule passage in Can't Hurt Me. He compares the mind's limit to the governor on a stock-car engine.

text: Sadly, most of us give up when we've only given around 40 percent of our maximum effort. Even when we feel like we've reached our absolute limit, we still have 60 percent more to give! That's the governor in action!
context: The three sentences that name the rule's arithmetic. He says the governor is what makes the early stop feel like an absolute limit.

text: The only way to move beyond your 40 percent is to callous your mind, day after day.
context: His close to that passage. Getting past the governor, he writes, is not a download. It is daily work.

text: You can have everything you want in life, but when you quit something that is meaningful to you, you will be haunted by it.
context: Pull quote from Christopher Keyes's profile in the January/February 2019 issue of Outside. Goggins said it by phone from Avalon, New Jersey.

text: This is why I say stay hard. Because when you weren't given the gifts, the only thing you can do in life is stay hard.
context: From the January 1, 2024 episode, How to Build Immense Inner Strength. He is explaining his own line, not repeating someone else.
